$comment: The rewrite of an HTML string to a call of interpolate, judged by both editors alike: a trim call after the literal stays inside the call, on the format; a multi-dollar literal keeps its prefix, so a $name that was text stays text; and a value in the body of a style, which interpolate refuses as a String, is passed as Trusted(...), where interpolate and Trusted are core's names in the file. The rewrite doubles a per cent sign the literal writes, and the %s fix passes one List, or a map to one, as one value. The format is the corpus's: fixes holds the whole source after each quick fix, in the order offered.

""".trimIndent()

x

""".trimIndent(), a, b).text

x

cases.name: the %s fix when the one value is visibly a List, which is one value
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(x: String, y: String) = interpolate("

$x %s

", listOf(y))

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $x before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the value to interpolate.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(x: String, y: String) = interpolate("

%s %s

", x, listOf(y))

issues.message: interpolate takes listOf(y) as one value and writes it whole, in brackets, escaped like any text. Write the elements out to pass them as the values.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(x: String, y: String) = interpolate("

$x %s

", y)

cases.name: the rewrite on a URL warning says interpolate refuses a URL that runs
cases.source: fun f(q: String) = "x"

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q at the start of href, so the value decides the scheme, and a javascript: URL runs. Escaping does not help: start the value with /, # or https://, or build the string with interpolate(...), which refuses a scheme that runs.
fixes: import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(q: String) = interpolate("x", q).text
